findings.title: Lockout threshold duplicated in the edge function
findings.question: ownership
findings.whatBreaks: The pause threshold (5) is the DB's fact (record_sign_in_failure enforces it); auth-event kept its own LOCK_THRESHOLD=5 to compute attempts-remaining. If the migration threshold were tuned, the enforced value and the displayed count would drift (decisions.md 'kept in sync' smell).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED before PR. Migration 011 adds sign_in_lock_threshold() (sole owner of 5), record_sign_in_failure reads it, and sign_in_attempts_remaining(p_hash) computes the count in the DB; auth-event drops LOCK_THRESHOLD and the extra read and calls the RPC. ADR-0007. pgTAP added (50_lockout.test.sql, 30_functions_and_grants.test.sql).

findings.title: Global sign-out ran after the throwing audit bookkeeping
findings.question: error-handling
findings.whatBreaks: completePasswordReset called onReset() (clear_sign_in_failures + log_event, which throw on a DB error) BEFORE signOutEverywhere(). If onReset threw, the password was already changed but the global sign-out was skipped and the route (no try/catch) returned a raw 500 - leaving pre-existing sessions alive after a recovery, the exact thing 'end all sessions' defends against.
findings.evidence: passwordReset.ts (pre-fix): onReset() awaited, then signOutEverywhere(); reset-password/route.ts has no try/catch. The edge change+event-atomic rule does not bind this Next route (ADR-0005).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED in a7ea266. signOutEverywhere() now runs BEFORE onReset(), and onReset is best-effort: it reports a DB failure via report() instead of throwing, so a bookkeeping hiccup cannot drop the (already-applied) session revocation. Unit test asserts sign-out precedes the bookkeeping.

findings.title: Completion event used subject_type 'profile' instead of the taxonomy 'admin'
findings.question: ownership
findings.whatBreaks: Every other log_event call (migrations 001/005/007) uses subject_type 'admin' for a profile subject, and the self-events RLS policy (migration 005) filters `subject_type = 'admin' and subject_id = auth.uid()`. findings.title: A reset writes two audit events (password_changed + password_reset_completed)
findings.question: ownership
findings.whatBreaks: updateUser({password}) fires the migration-007 auth.users trigger, which writes auth.password_changed; the app also writes auth.password_reset_completed. Two rows per reset.
findings.evidence: migrations/007_display_name_trigger.sql:26-27 (auth.password_changed on encrypted_password change); passwordReset.ts onReset log_event auth.password_reset_completed.
findings.resolution: WAIVED (intended). They are distinct facts: the trigger records the DB-level password change; the app event records the reset-flow completion with actor/ip/request context that ADR-0008 requires. Each row has a single DB writer (log_event), so there is no dual-ownership. Noted in a code comment.

findings.title: completeReplacement old-factor removal non-atomic / asymmetric reporting
findings.question: error-handling
findings.evidence: mfa.ts completeReplacement: the stale-factor unenroll loop ran AFTER the new factor was verified but was unguarded, so a Supabase error threw -> the route showed 'failed / nothing changed' while the new device was already active (briefly two verified factors). RESOLVED in-branch (commit after review): the removal is now best-effort (try/catch + report('warning',...), still returns 'replaced'), mirroring the sibling unverified-factor cleanup; covered by mfa.test.ts 'still returns replaced when the old factor can't be removed'.

reviewContext: Fresh-context subagent (general-purpose) reviewed the committed diff against decisions.md, the functions/components AGENTS.md, and ADR-0009 (treated as intended architecture). 21 production files × 4 questions = 84 cells (83 cleared, 1 F1 since resolved). Security-sensitive properties confirmed by evidence: RLS is_aal2() is the authorization boundary (route gate is UX-only); verifier.ts and exchangeReauthIdentity never clobber the live session; the HMAC re-auth marker is server-secret-signed, user-bound, expiring, constant-time (proven by reauthMarker.test.ts); replacement re-authenticates before touching any factor and keeps exactly one verified factor.
